newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vows to govern from political center.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vows to govern from political center.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, making his first major speech since winning re-election, on Wednesday said balancing the federal budget was his top priority and pledged to govern from the political centre.

"Today the clamour of political conflict has subsided, a new landscape is taking shape. The answer is clear: the centre can hold, the centre has held and the American people are demanding that it continue to do so," Clinton said in a speech to the moderate Democratic Leadership Council.

Clinton noted that when he spoke at the group's annual conference a year ago, the government had been on the verge of shutting down because of a bitter dispute between the Democrats and the Republicans over how to balance the budget.
He said that balancing the budget was his top priority and reiterated his recent calls for the Democrats and Republicans to cooperate on this, and other matters.

"Our first task is to finish the job of balancing the budget," Clinton said, citing other challenges such as making the new welfare reform law work, improving national education and bringing about campaign finance reform.

"They can be achieved only if there is a vital American centre where there is cooperation across lines of party and philosophy," Clinton added. "This is an irreplaceable moment for breaking new ground in America."
